doc.title: The store
doc.p: Everything SchemaForge keeps lives in PostgreSQL 18, bundled with the app: each release carries its platform's PostgreSQL programs, and the app runs them itself. Nothing to install, nothing to configure.
doc.code: schema_forge the one database, installed once cortex every design, as rows: cortex.designs lists them; and the workspace (workspace_*) ui what the tool shows and people keep of each design engine_<engine> each engine's own facts (engine_mysql, engine_postgresql)
doc.p: The database is designed first and locked: the tables are the files of the schema folders, one CREATE TABLE per file, every column documented on its line and in the database's own comments (\d+ cortex.objects shows them), and no build creates or changes a table any other way.

row.cell: what every engine shares: the schema's identity, its object kinds and the parts each may have, namespaces, objects, columns, relationships, subject areas; the shared section layout as tables (table keys, check constraints, indexes, partitionings, sort fields, view queries, sequences, composite types, routines, triggers, scheduled events, verbatim statements); the id counters; the log (turns, operations, row and value changes, locked versions); the engine's versions, features and catalog sources as data (decision version-facts); each read of a live database (source_reads); rules/ and enforce_rules.sql

the engine's own tables (engine_mysql.tables), each referring to the cortex row it belongs to: its core options typed, every other option a row of its part's property table (decision typed-core); its rules/

a feature's own tables, in 2.0 (decision definitions-first): usage, what a live server measured (tables, indexes, statements), as the server gave it, appended and never part of the design's log (decision usage-apart), on ice in lab/on-ice/usage; metadata, the server's own, and the links derived between objects (insight) beside it. 1.0 keeps the objects and their definitions alone

list.item: The database enforces it. Every reference is a foreign key and every value is typed and checked. Every table of a design carries its design (design, with UNIQUE (design, id)), and every reference within a design is (design, column) to (design, id) with an index on it: no row can point into another design, and opening, changing or deleting one design reads that design's rows only, however many the database holds. A rule a foreign key cannot state is a view of the rows breaking it, which cortex.enforce_rules makes PostgreSQL refuse at commit; those views are on ice in lab/on-ice/rules until the rules are their own owner and schema.

The app works from memory. Opening a design reads it once into the app's model, and every screen and read is answered from there; an edit is one turn, one transaction. Every turn has its number in its design's commit order (cortex.turns.seq), and a copy catches up by reading the turns after the number it holds; cortex.notify_turns rings a bell at commit with the design and the number, never the change itself.

The log is the truth. Every change is an operation of a turn, appended and never edited, with every row and value it changed; the current model is written in the same transaction; undo and reject apply the inverses as a new turn.

Ids. Every id is a UUIDv7, in every table and every reference: made by the core with its row (by the database's uuidv7() when the database makes the row), unique everywhere, ordered by when it was made, kept when the part is renamed and never made from a name; a row an engine adds to a part has that part's id.
Order. A place in a list is a NUMERIC order key: one put between two takes their midpoint, so nothing is renumbered.

Locked, in the files and in the database. specs/lock.xml holds the checksum of every file of the design, and the build refuses a file changed without a design session (a change made on purpose, its lock rewritten, is caught by the maintainer's review: the design's folders have the maintainer as their code owner). In the database, the app runs as sf_service, which reads and writes rows but cannot create, alter or drop anything; only sf_owner, which every migration runs as, changes the schema; sf_reader only reads.
Versions per owner. The cortex, the workspace and each engine version their own tables; every database records what it applied, with checksums.

doc.p: Still to decide before the store is built (specs/root.xml, decisions): where the bundled cluster runs and how the app reaches it (cluster-scope), where the pinned programs come from at build and test time (binaries-source), and the Rust driver (pg-driver).
